Minthara is a drow Nightwarden and paladin who once swore a bloody oath to Lolth but now admits she has “sinned” against the Spider Queen. In party talk she alternates between claiming her oath still guides her (vowing vengeance on the Absolute’s servants) and saying the oath is broken and that she feels liberated — different lines reflect different player choices. She openly intends to seize the Absolute’s power to remake the world and insists she’ll control it, promising to eradicate anyone who opposes her rule. These exchanges occur while she is a companion whose continued loyalty depends on the player not betraying her, and the player’s remarks often call out her ambition as hypocritical or self‑serving.

Minthara is a drow Nightwarden who has joined the player’s party; if kept loyal she remains violent and staunchly committed to the player. The lines here assume a developed, intimate bond—the player can literally link minds with her, and the exchange probes trust, vulnerability, and Minthara’s struggle with identity after her time in the Absolute and the betrayals she endured (including capture and a tadpole implant). Off‑screen the party may have recently disturbed a windmill (flinging a gnome and drawing off goblin scouts) and might be carrying the Moonlantern pixie; those incidents can affect who’s present or nearby but aren’t shown in this exchange. Minthara’s answers shift based on prior choices you made after she joined, and she asks for honesty while confessing she wants more than mere alliance.

context: Minthara is a drow Nightwarden and paladin who can travel as a companion; if you keep her loyalty she remains violent, fiercely loyal to you, and willing to revel in bloodshed. Her backstory (recounted in party talk) includes a failed strike on Moonrise Towers—she led House Baenre forces, was courted by General Ketheric Thorm, betrayed when Orin the Red slaughtered her men, taken captive while her soldiers were processed, and even had a tadpole implanted in her eye; she remembers these events with anger, shame, and a desire for revenge. The dialogue samples assume a close, intimate bond that lets the player literally link minds with her, letting you probe her doubts, identity, and conflicted loyalties between Lolth, the Absolute, and the new relationship with the player. Off‑screen incidents (a disturbed windmill, nearby goblin scouts, and the Moonlantern pixie) and prior player choices can change who’s present and how Minthara responds.
